narrative.overview:
The site is a working one-bit desktop, not a page dressed as one. Every surface is ink or paper, and every grey is an ordered dither of the two. Content lives in windows: white rectangles with a 2px ink frame, a striped title bar, a square close box and a hard, unblurred drop shadow. The windows sit on a desktop whose ground is a live dither field, and they behave as windows did: they drag by their title bars, roll up to their title bars, and zoom open out of icons. The documentation pages use the same chrome, but read on plain paper, in the reading face.

One pixel of this world is two CSS pixels (`--px`). Borders, rules, shadows, outlines and pattern cells are whole multiples of it, so lines stay as crisp as the dithers next to them. Patterns are SVG tiles rendered with `image-rendering: pixelated`, never CSS gradients, because a gradient's stops antialias into a blurred grey. Interaction comes from the medium's own grammar: pressing and hovering invert, a selected icon or row is drawn in inverse video, focus is marching ants, the current item in a list is a highlighted row, and the item that comes next wears animated marching ants.

The world keeps the medium's generic grammar and drops everything that belongs to Apple: no Apple logo, no Chicago or Geneva, no Finder, Trash or happy-computer icons. Every icon, the logo and the favicon are OmniBuild's own 16 by 16 pixel grids. Nothing imitates Apple's or Google's sites or product art.
keyCharacteristics: Two values, ink and paper; greys only as 12, 25, 50 and 75% ordered dithers.
Dark mode is inverse video: ink and paper swap, and the system stays one-bit.
Windows with 2px frames, striped title bars, square close boxes and hard ink shadows.
Three faces with fixed jobs: Jersey 10 for display, Tiny5 for chrome and labels, Atkinson Hyperlegible Next for every sentence and for the docs pages whole.
Motion is stepped and pixel-whole: XOR outlines, zoom rectangles, marching ants, barber-pole progress.

rules.name: The Two Values Rule
rules.body: Ink and paper are the only colours. A grey, a tint, an opacity fade or a coloured accent is never introduced; a tone between them is a dither tile at a whole multiple of `--px`, rendered pixelated.

rules.name: The Inverse Video Rule
rules.body: Emphasis and state are shown by swapping ink and paper: hover, press, selection, the active nav item, the current step, table heads and notices. Dark mode is the same swap applied to the whole screen.

rules.name: The Clear Glyph Rule
rules.body: No dither, stripe or pattern ever sits under glyphs. A title on a striped bar sits on its own paper slab; an icon label sits on paper over the dither ground; inline code is a 1px ink frame, not a shaded chip; a read-only field carries its 50% dither only in a band inside its frame.

rules.name: The Five-Pixel Rule
rules.body: Tiny5 is drawn on a 5px grid and is set only at 15px (`--pixel-s`) and 20px (`--pixel-m`), so every stem is a whole number of pixels. It is never bolded, never set at other sizes and never used for running copy.

rules.name: The Sentence Face Rule
rules.body: Every sentence, status lines included, is set in Atkinson Hyperlegible Next. Tiny5 is for words and labels; when a sentence sits in chrome it is Atkinson at 600.

rules.name: The Reading Page Rule
rules.body: A docs page is set entirely in Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, its headings and navigation included, and so is the landing page's roadmap, which summarises the plan. The pixel faces stop at the site's chrome: the menu bar, window title bars and the footer.

rules.name: The One-Bit Syntax Rule
rules.body: Code has no colours to tell tokens apart, so keywords, builtins, tags and selectors are bold, comments are italic and deletions are struck through, in ink on paper.

rules.name: The Hard Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are solid ink at `--px` multiples (2, 4, 6px) with no blur and no spread. One-bit screens had no blur, so neither does this world.

rules.name: The Window Shade Rule
rules.body: Every close box does something a reader can undo. When the page can reopen the window (the demonstration reopens from its icon), the close box closes it with zoom rectangles back to the icon. Otherwise it rolls the window up to its title bar, and a second press rolls it down. A section is never lost to a click.

dos: **Do** use only `{colors.ink}` and `{colors.paper}`, and make every intermediate tone a dither tile at a whole multiple of `--px` with `image-rendering: pixelated`.
**Do** put content in windows: 2px ink frame, striped title bar with the title on a paper slab, square close box, 6px hard shadow.
**Do** show state by inverting: hover, press, selection, current row and active item swap ink and paper.
**Do** set Tiny5 at 15px or 20px only, and every sentence in Atkinson Hyperlegible Next (600 in chrome).
**Do** show focus as a 2px dashed outline (marching ants), and the next or selected item with animated ants where the page can animate them.
**Do** show a disabled control with a dotted frame and a solid label.
**Do** give every close box an undoable action: close when the page can reopen the window, roll up otherwise.
**Do** draw new icons as OmniBuild's own pixel grids (`#` ink, `o` paper, `.` transparent) at whole-number scales.
donts: **Don't** use any colour, grey hex, opacity fade, gradient or blur.
**Don't** put a dither, stripe or pattern under text; frame it instead.
**Don't** round UI corners or soften shadows; shadows are solid ink offsets of 2, 4 or 6px.
**Don't** use the Apple logo, Chicago or Geneva, or Finder, Trash or happy-computer icons, or imitate Apple's or Google's sites or product art.
**Don't** use icon fonts or glyph icons; Docusaurus's external-link arrows are hidden for that reason.
**Don't** set Tiny5 for running copy, bolded, or at sizes other than 15px and 20px.
**Don't** turn status into a badge or pill; it is a printed line.
**Don't** let a window grab touch drags; on touch the page scrolls.
